pip-compile.description: Manage the hash-pinned docs lock: read docs/requirements.txt's pip-compile header, bump deps in docs/requirements.in, and regenerate the lock with --generate-hashes.

customManagers.description: Track the zizmor version pinned in security.yml's `uv tool install`. It is installed via uv at run time, so neither the github-actions nor any package manager sees it.

Track the pinned actionlint (workflow linter) release in actionlint.yml via github-releases. Renovate bumps ONLY ACTIONLINT_VERSION; the download URL derives from it in the run-script, so version + URL can't drift. The adjacent ACTIONLINT_SHA256 is NOT auto-updated (github-releases exposes the git-tag digest, not the release tarball's checksum), so a bump PR carries a stale hash until it is refreshed by hand from the release's checksums.txt — the actionlint job's own `sha256sum -c` then fails loudly on the mismatch, so a stale hash can never silently ship. Held for review by the base custom.regex rule (no auto-merge, `vendored` label); scratchsmith has no pin-refresh script, so no postUpgradeTask.

Track cargo-zigbuild, the cross-linker build tool pinned in taiki-e/install-action's `tool:` input in ci.yml and knope-release.yml. github-actions pins the install-action `uses:` SHA but does not parse the `tool:` value, so the pinned build-tool version was invisible. crates.io datasource. Held for review (vendored) by the base policy — a deliberate heads-up before the release build tool moves, matching the actionlint pin.

packageRules.description: Hold the MSRV job's Rust toolchain at the DECLARED minimum (Cargo.toml rust-version = 1.96). ci.yml's `build (MSRV 1.96)` job exists to prove the crate still builds on that floor; letting Renovate track it toward stable silently stops verifying the MSRV. Bump it only alongside a deliberate rust-version raise. (scratchsmith is the only repo in the fleet with a pinned MSRV job; siblings track stable.)

Supply-chain cooldown: soak every update for 7 days before it may merge (auto-merges included), so a freshly-published or yanked release can't land the same day it appears — fitting for a supply-chain tool. Security fixes stay immediate via the shared default's vulnerabilityAlerts (minimumReleaseAge: null).
Digests and pins carry no release date, so the release-age soak can never pass and Renovate would suppress or never merge them. Exempt them from the soak.

docs/requirements.txt is a hash-pinned pip-compile lock (generated from docs/requirements.in). The pip-compile manager updates the .in and regenerates the lock WITH hashes; pip_requirements must NOT touch the lock or it would bump a version without regenerating --hash lines, breaking the --require-hashes install. Keep it disabled for that file.
Docs toolchain (mkdocs-material + mike + transitive deps) bumps land in one PR via the pip-compile lock; chore(deps) keeps the conventional-title check happy.
